name: Search for new high-mass dilepton resonances and nonresonant phenomena (2016–2018 data)
notes: Numerical mass limits are quoted in the body of the paper, not in the abstract that was fetched, so no key_value is recorded.

significance.note: An exclusion; the paper reports no significant deviation from the standard model.
significance.quote: No significant deviation is observed with respect to the SM background expectations.

summary.plain: CMS searched its 2016–2018 13 TeV data (up to 140 fb^-1) for electron or muon pairs from a heavy new particle and saw no significant deviation from the Standard Model background. The abstract says the limits are the most stringent to date on the masses of various spin-1 particles, spin-2 gravitons (Randall–Sundrum model) and spin-1 dark-matter mediators.
summary.technical: Dielectron and dimuon mass spectra from up to 140 fb^-1 of 13 TeV data (2016–2018): no significant deviation from the standard model background expectations; upper limits on narrow resonances relative to the Z boson (most stringent lower limits to date on masses of various spin-1 particles, Randall–Sundrum spin-2 gravitons and spin-1 dark-matter mediators), lower limits on the ultraviolet cutoff for four-fermion contact interactions and the ADD model, and a lepton-flavour-universality test at the TeV scale, which the abstract says is done for the first time.

title: Search for resonant and nonresonant new phenomena in high-mass dilepton final states at sqrt(s) = 13 TeV
why_it_matters: The abstract reports no significant deviation from the standard model background expectations; lower limits on the masses of various spin-1 particles, Randall–Sundrum gravitons and spin-1 mediators between the standard model and dark matter; lower limits on the ultraviolet cutoff for contact interactions and the ADD large-extra-dimension model; and a TeV-scale test of lepton flavour universality.
